maya (sec-eng): Heads-up: we got a customer asking about GCP Cloud KMS for Private deployments. They want guidance on service accounts, key rings, least-privilege IAM, envelope encryption, and rotation best-practices.

sam (platform): Great — we should recommend an approach that avoids giving broad project roles. Prefer key-level grants and service account impersonation.

jess (customer-ops): Customer runs Private in their VPC and asked if Redwood needs a SA in their project or if they should create a key and share access.

maya (sec-eng): Recommendation summary first: 1) Customer creates KeyRing + CryptoKey in their project. 2) Customer creates a dedicated service account for Redwood usage (or allows our infra SA to be impersonated via Workload Identity). 3) Grant only roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the specific CryptoKey to that SA. 4) Use envelope encryption: DEKs generated locally, wrapped with KMS (as a best-practice). 5) Rotate keys by creating new CryptoKeyVersions and update configuration; retain previous keys for unwrap during rollout. 6) Enable Cloud Audit Logs for KMS (admin/data access) and export to their log sink.

sam (platform): Adding detail: For Private deployments running inside the customer's GCP project, the simplest path: create a service account in the customer project that Redwood's runtime will use. Example minimal IAM binding (apply to resource-level CryptoKey):

```
# create key ring and key (customer project)
gcloud kms keyrings create redwood-keyring --location=us-central1 --project=customer-project-id

gcloud kms keys create redwood-key --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-keyring --purpose=encryption --rotation-period=2592000s # 30d example

# grant encrypt/decrypt to the runtime service account
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding redwood-key --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-keyring \
  --member=serviceAccount:REPLACE_WITH_SA_EMAIL --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```

Note: use resource-level binding to avoid granting project-wide KMS roles.

jess (customer-ops): What about using Redwood-managed SA in our project vs. us creating the SA? Which is safer?

maya (sec-eng): Safer is customer-created SA in their project that Redwood is allowed to impersonate, or simply provide long-lived SA credentials if they accept that risk (we generally discourage long-lived keys). If the deployment is fully customer-run (on-prem or customer GKE), they can create a SA and give its key to the runtime locally. If Redwood will run control-plane components outside their project, prefer Workload Identity Federation / impersonation so we don't exchange static keys.

sam (platform): If customers want minimal privileges, they can also add an IAM condition restricting usage by principal namespace or time. Example IAM condition to limit usages from specific service account: not strictly necessary for resource-level binding but useful for defense-in-depth.

jess (customer-ops): How should envelope encryption be implemented in our stack?

maya (sec-eng): Envelope pattern we recommend: 1) Runtime generates a fresh DEK (symmetric key) per logical tenant or per file. 2) Data is encrypted locally with DEK (AES-GCM). 3) DEK is wrapped (Encrypt) with Cloud KMS CryptoKey. 4) Store wrapped DEK alongside ciphertext. On read: unwrap with KMS (Decrypt) to get DEK, then decrypt locally. This reduces KMS QPS and keeps plaintext keys ephemeral in memory only.

sam (platform): Implementation tips: - Cache unwrapped DEKs for a short TTL in RAM only (no disk). - Use KMS asymmetric keys only for specific use-cases; symmetric keys (CryptoKey with purpose ENCRYPT_DECRYPT) are typical. - Watch KMS hourly quotas; envelope reduces calls.

jess (customer-ops): Rotation: customer asked how to rotate keys without downtime or losing access to previous data.

maya (sec-eng): Rotation approach: create new CryptoKeyVersion and update the config to use the new version to wrap new DEKs. Keep old versions enabled for decrypt (KMS supports decrypt with previous versions). Steps: 1) Create new key version or new key (if you prefer); 2) config change to make new version the primary; 3) gradually rewrap DEKs or re-encrypt data if customer wants all data rewrapped. Always retain old key versions until you rewrap everything.

sam (platform): Example commands for rotation (primary rotation via gcloud):

```
# create new version
gcloud kms keys versions create 1 --key=redwood-key --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-keyring

# set new primary (if using CryptoKey update)
# For automatic rotation, set rotation schedule on key creation (rotationPeriod)
```

Note: KMS supports explicit disable/destroy lifecycle on versions; do NOT destroy versions while decrypts still needed.

jess (customer-ops): Audit logs — what should we instruct customers to monitor?

maya (sec-eng): Enable Admin Activity and Data Access audit logs for Cloud KMS. Filter for: Encrypt, Decrypt, CreateCryptoKeyVersion, DestroyCryptoKeyVersion, SetIamPolicy, etc. Recommend export to a log sink (BigQuery / PubSub) and hooking to SIEM/Alerting for anomalous Decrypt calls or IAM changes. Also alert on grant changes to the crypto key resource.

sam (platform): Also recommend using CMEK naming conventions and tagging keys (labels) with owner/team and purpose. That makes audits and automated policies easier.

jess (customer-ops): Customer also asked about cross-project access (key in infra project, runtime in customer project). Is that supported?

maya (sec-eng): Cross-project is supported: grant the runtime SA from the runtime project the cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter role on the key resource in the key's project. But cross-project access complicates audit ownership and increases blast radius; prefer keys in the same project as runtime.

infra-bot: deploy-check: KMS policy lint passed for redwood-keyring in customer-project-id (simulated). :white_check_mark:

maya (sec-eng): Misc operational notes: - Recommend customers keep a dedicated key ring per product boundary. - Use labels and docs to track rotation schedule. - If using HSM (Cloud HSM backing), document SLA/latency tradeoffs. - Test restore/unwrap process during onboarding.

sam (platform): For Private deployments we'll add a section to onboarding docs with exact gcloud snippets, least-privilege IAM bindings, and audit sink examples. We should also add a checklist: (1) create key ring + key, (2) grant SA encrypt/decrypt on key, (3) enable audit logs + export, (4) provide SA email or configure Workload Identity, (5) schedule rotation.

jess (customer-ops): I'll draft the onboarding email and include an optional script to create the resources.

maya (sec-eng): Thanks — if you want, I can review the script for IAM least-privilege and add a short threat model paragraph about key compromise. Quick threat notes: if SA creds leak, attacker can unwrap DEKs — mitigate with short-lived credentials, IAM conditions, and alerting.

sam (platform): One more runtime note: use Google client libraries with a short-lived token flow and set sensible grpc/http timeouts when calling KMS to avoid hanging requests.

maya (sec-eng): OK — assigning follow-ups: jess: draft onboarding + script; sam: add doc page; maya: review script + add threat model + audit alerting examples.

jess (customer-ops): on it.

sam (platform): I'll spin up PR for docs later today.

maya (sec-eng): Closing thread — thanks everyone. :lock:
